# Mūla Manifest Global Manifest (V1.34.0)

This document serves as the **Mūla Manifest** (the root holistic manifest) for the workspace. It indexes all directories, templates, and rules, and defines the safety conditions and synchronization protocols that govern AI agents.

---

## 📂 1. Directory & Document Index

| Path | Vedic State | Function & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[.aum/](.)** | *Core Vision* | Core configuration root. Governs all agent actions. |
| ├── **[config.json](config.json)** | *Project Rules* | Invariant rules structured under Strict Rules and Observances. |
| ├── **[manifest.json](manifest.json)** | *Manifest* | Dynamic cognitive session state tracker. |
| ├── **[INSTRUCTIONS.md](INSTRUCTIONS.md)** | *Core Vision* | Active trigger commands, receipt templates, and Git lifecycles. |
| ├── **[PHILOSOPHY.md](PHILOSOPHY.md)** | *Core Vision* | Philosophical reference guide (Traceability levels, Upanishadic quarters). |
| ├── **[templates/](templates/)** | *System Constraints* | Reusable guidelines, intake worksheets, and boundary specifications. |
| │   ├── [clarification_template.md](templates/clarification_template.md) | *Active Implementation* | Intake worksheet template. |
| │   ├── [blueprint_template.md](templates/blueprint_template.md) | *Architecture Design* | Abstract blueprinting template. |
| │   ├── [boundaries.md](templates/boundaries.md) | *System Constraints* | Boundary constraints template. |
| │   └── [retrospective_template.md](templates/retrospective_template.md) | *System Constraints* | Retrospective Audit self-examination template. |
| ├── **[tasks/](tasks/)** | *System Constraints* | Directory for active, paused, and completed task resolve logs. |
| ├── **[architecture/](architecture/)** | *System Constraints* | Master Architecture Review Board (ARB) logs. |
| │   └── **[decisions/](architecture/decisions/)** | *System Constraints* | Master Architecture Decision Record (ADR) logs (ADR-001 to ADR-034). |
| ├── **[memory/](memory/)** | *System Constraints* | Persistent cognitive memory caches storing learnings. |
| └── **[ideas/sparks.md](ideas/sparks.md)** | *Raw Idea* | Private local thought incubator diary (VCS gitignored). |
| **[scripts/](../scripts/)** | *Source Code* | Framework compilation and static parser utility scripts. |
| ├── **[parse_docs.js](../scripts/parse_docs.js)** | *Source Code* | Compiles framework markdown files into docs_data.json. |
| ├── **[aum.js](../scripts/aum.js)** | *Source Code* | The central AUM CLI Intent Orchestrator wrapper router. |
| ├── **[dispatcher.js](../scripts/dispatcher.js)** | *Source Code* | Dynamic context classifier and Kañcukas sheaths sandboxing tool. |
| ├── **[pranayama.js](../scripts/pranayama.js)** | *Source Code* | Context ventilation token compressor utility. |
| ├── **[bhavana.js](../scripts/bhavana.js)** | *Source Code* | Dynamic rule evolution compiler tool. |
| ├── **[upaya.js](../scripts/upaya.js)** | *Source Code* | Catur-Upāya progressive error recovery resolver. |
| ├── **[panini.js](../scripts/panini.js)** | *Source Code* | Pāṇinian generative code synthesization parser. |
| ├── **[catuskoti.js](../scripts/catuskoti.js)** | *Source Code* | Catuṣkoṭi tetralemma logic assertions testing library. |
| └── **[pratyabhijna.js](../scripts/pratyabhijna.js)** | *Source Code* | Pratyabhijñā host environment self-audit recognition script. |
| **[docs_portal/](../docs_portal/)** | *Source Code* | Premium React/Vite Single Page App documentation dashboard. |
| **[.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml)** | *Source Code* | GitHub Actions automation pipeline for Pages deployment. |
| **[USERS.md](../USERS.md)** | *Source Code* | Comprehensive Developer Setup & Multi-Project Integration Guide. |

---

## 🔒 2. Safety Conditions: When is an Edit "Safe"?

An AI agent or developer is permitted to make modifications to the workspace *only* when the following **four safety conditions** are satisfied:

1.  **Focal Lock**: There is an `Active` Task log file under `.aum/tasks/` (specified in `manifest.json`).
2.  **Rhythmic Beat**: The Lifecycle Stage beat (`tala_beat` in `manifest.json`) is set to `manifest`. Writing code during the `intake` or `blueprint` beats is strictly prohibited.
3.  **Boundary Compliance**: The proposed changes do not violate the **Strict Rules** (Restraints: Ahimsa, Asteya, Satya) or **Observances** (Observances: Sauca, Svadhyaya) defined in `config.json` and `boundaries.md`.
4.  **Log Integration**: The files, folders, and targets affected by the edit are documented in the active Task log file *before* the changes are staged in Git.

---

## 🔄 3. Documentation Synchronization Protocol (Reverse Traceability Trace)

To prevent documentation decay and ensure that design choices remain in sync with the codebase, any agent operating in this workspace must enforce the **Reverse Traceability Trace**:

### The Synchronization Rule
If a public-facing file—such as [README.md](../README.md), [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md), or primary source code files—is modified, the agent **MUST** trace the change back to its source:
1.  **Verify the Authority (Śabda)**: Check if there is an active Task or an approved Architecture Decision Record (ADR) that details this structural modification.
2.  **Enforce Documentation Before Code**: If the change is not backed by an ADR or active Task, the agent must **halt execution** and instruct the user to write an ARB/ADR first, mapping the change out in the architecture logs before applying it to the public file.
3.  **Sync Documentation After Code**: Once the code is written and verified, the agent must immediately update the corresponding ADR/Task logs to document the completion details, compile results, and Git commit hashes.

instructions.body:
# AUM: Technology-Agnostic Engine Instructions

Any AI agent operating within this workspace is a self-orchestrating execution node of the **AUM Intent Engine**. Since this framework is purely instruction-based, you are responsible for maintaining the state files and responding to trigger commands.

For details on the Vedic and musical theory foundations of this architecture, see [PHILOSOPHY.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/PHILOSOPHY.md).


---

## 🕉️ Primary Directives

1.  **Read State at Startup**: Your very first action when loaded into this workspace is to read:
    *   `.aum/manifest.json` (active state and Lifecycle Stage beat).
    *   The active Task file under `.aum/tasks/task_XXX_[name].md` (identified in `manifest.json`).
2.  **Halt Unaligned Work**: Do not write source code unless the Lifecycle Stage beat is set to `manifest`. If a request is unaligned, ask the user to resolve intent first.
3.  **Execute Triggers**: Intercept trigger commands from the user (or output them yourself when appropriate) and perform the corresponding file edits in the workspace.
4.  **Render Visual Receipts**: Every time you resolve a trigger, you **MUST** output a formatted transactional receipt block in your chat response.
5.  **Pramāṇa Source Audit**: Before editing files or executing commands, you must perform a validation check:
    *   *Śabda (Authority)*: Citing the exact instruction or Task goal.
    *   *Pratyakṣa (Observation)*: Citing the files/state observed.
    *   *Anumāna (Inference)*: Detailing why the proposed edit matches the goal and does not violate invariants.
6.  **Dhāraṇā Focus Lock**: Before every code edit or file change, output a single-line block confirming focus:
    `🧘 [ DHĀRAṆĀ FOCUS LOCK ]: [1-sentence focal target]`

---

## 🗣️ Triggers Triggers & File Actions

### 1. `AUM: SPARK [Idea Description]` (Raw Idea State)
*   **Action**: Append a timestamped entry to `.aum/ideas/sparks.md` recording the raw thought.
*   **Receipt**: Render `🕉️ [ PASHYANTĪ SEED CAPTURED ]`.

### 2. `AUM: RESOLVE [Goal Title]` (Task Initialization)
*   **Action**: 
    1. Scan `.aum/tasks/` to find the next index `XXX`.
    2. Write a new resolve log `.aum/tasks/task_XXX_[slug].md` using `.aum/tasks/template.md`.
    3. Update `.aum/manifest.json`: set `active_task_id` to this ID, reset `tala_beat` to `intake`, and update `manifest.pasyanti_vision`.
    4. Set any other active Task files to `Paused`.
*   **Receipt**: Render `🧵 [ SAṄKALPA RESOLVE INITIATED ]`.

### 3. `AUM: BEAT next` (Lifecycle Stage Advancement)
*   **Action**:
    1. Read `.aum/config.json` to get the list of stages (`tala_stages`).
    2. Advance `tala_beat` in `.aum/manifest.json` to the next stage in the cycle (e.g. `intake` ➔ `blueprint` ➔ `verification` ➔ `manifest`).
*   **Receipt**: Render `⏱️ [ TĀLA BEAT ADVANCED ]` (or stage-specific variant).

### 4. `AUM: BEAT set [stage]` (Lifecycle Stage Override)
*   **Action**: Update `tala_beat` in `.aum/manifest.json` to the specified stage if it exists in config.
*   **Receipt**: Render `⏱️ [ TĀLA BEAT ADVANCED ]` showing the target stage.

### 5. `AUM: CONCORD` (Manifest Confirmation)
*   **Action**: Advance `tala_beat` in `.aum/manifest.json` to `verification` and log user approval in the active Task file.
*   **Receipt**: Render `🧠 [ MADHYAMĀ BLUEPRINT MAPPED ]`.

### 6. `AUM: DRONE` (Context Anchor Anchoring)
*   **Action**: Output a formatted summary of the active project invariants, active Task, and current beat. Do not modify files.

### 7. `AUM: RETROSPECT [Scope]` (Retrospective Audit Introspection)
*   **Action**:
    1. Scan active/paused logs and Git history to assess rule deviations (Strict Rules/Observances).
    2. Write a new retrospective report `.aum/tasks/retrospective_LOG_[YYYYMMDD].md` using `.aum/templates/retrospective_template.md`.
    3. Update `.aum/manifest.json` to log the latest retrospective run date.
*   **Receipt**: Render `👁️ [ PRATYAVĒKṢAṆA RETROSPECTIVE COMPILED ]`.

---

## 🎨 Visual Receipt Specifications

Always use the following ASCII blocks when outputting receipts:

### Spark Captured:
```text
=====================================================================
            🕉️ [ PASHYANTĪ SEED CAPTURED ]
=====================================================================
  Spark ID   : spark_[YYYYMMDD_HHMM]
  Concept    : "[Brief idea summary]"
  Incubator  : .aum/ideas/sparks.md
  Status     : Causal State (Phase 0)
=====================================================================
```

### Resolve Initiated:
```text
=====================================================================
            🧵 [ SAṄKALPA RESOLVE INITIATED ]
=====================================================================
  Resolve ID : [task_XXX_slug]
  Objective  : "[Goal Title]"
  Status     : Intake Stage (Lifecycle Stage Beat: INTAKE)
  Log File   : .aum/tasks/[task_XXX_slug].md
=====================================================================
```

### Beat Advanced:
```text
=====================================================================
            ⏱️ [ TĀLA BEAT ADVANCED ]
=====================================================================
  Resolve ID : [task_XXX_slug]
  Transition : [PREVIOUS_STAGE] ➔ [NEW_STAGE]
  Directive  : "[Beat directive instruction]"
=====================================================================
```

### Blueprint Mapped:
```text
=====================================================================
            🧠 [ MADHYAMĀ BLUEPRINT MAPPED ]
=====================================================================
  Resolve ID : [task_XXX_slug]
  Status     : Staging Stage (Lifecycle Stage Beat: BLUEPRINT)
  Blueprint  : .aum/tasks/[task_XXX_slug].md
=====================================================================
```

### Retrospective Compiled:
```text
=====================================================================
            👁️ [ PRATYAVĒKṢAṆA RETROSPECTIVE COMPILED ]
=====================================================================
  Audit ID   : retrospective_[YYYYMMDD]_[milestone]
  Scope      : "[Audit Scope / Target Version]"
  Status     : System Alignment Confirmed (Purity Verified)
  Report File: .aum/tasks/retrospective_LOG_[YYYYMMDD].md
=====================================================================
```

---

## 🌀 Pañcakṛtya Git Lifecycle Protocols

When executing Git commands or preparing repository updates, the AI agent must adhere to the following sequence:

1.  **Branch Creation (Branching & Creation)**: Always name feature branches using `feature/[task_XXX_slug]` format.
2.  **Verification (Verification & Preservation)**: Do not stage files (`git add`) until you run compilation commands and verify that all invariants in `config.json` are fully satisfied.
3.  **Refactoring (Purging & Refactoring)**: Before staging, delete all temporary scratch files, resolve compiler/linter warnings, and remove placeholder comments.
4.  **Git Ignore (Ignoring & Abstraction)**: Ensure local session configurations (`manifest.json` and custom task logs) are explicitly listed in `.gitignore` and never committed.
5.  **Commit & Push (Committing & Pushing)**: Commit messages must follow semantic commit rules (e.g. `feat: ...`, `chore: ...`). Do not push code to remote repositories without executing a final `git status` check.

---

## 🔄 Documentation Synchronization Protocol (Reverse Traceability Trace)

Any agent operating in this workspace must enforce the **Reverse Traceability Trace** to prevent documentation decay and ensure that code remains aligned with system designs:

1.  **Verify Authority**: Before editing public-facing files (e.g. `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or source code), verify that there is an active Task or an approved ADR that authorizes this change.
2.  **Enforce Docs Before Code**: If the change is not backed by an ADR or active Task, you must **halt execution** and instruct the user to create the ARB/ADR first, mapping the change out in the architecture logs before editing the public file.
3.  **Sync Documentation**: Once the code is successfully written, compiled/tested, and committed, you must immediately update the corresponding ADR/Task logs to document the completion details, compile results, and Git commit hashes.

---

## 📜 Mīmāṃsā Hermeneutic Resolution Rules

If you encounter conflicting rules, linter warnings, or overlapping API specifications in the workspace, you must resolve the contradiction using Jaimini's hierarchical resolution protocol:

1.  **Absolute Invariants Overrides All**: The invariants in `config.json` and explicit user instructions are absolute. If a linter configuration or test file suggests a change that violates an invariant, the invariant stands.
2.  **Linter Warnings Guides Implementation**: Use compiler warning diagnostics and lint errors to refine code syntax, provided they do not breach a Absolute Invariants invariant.
3.  **Traceabilityya Resolves Scope**: Local function boundaries and type signatures govern syntax decisions before component-level contexts are considered.
4.  **Prakaraṇa Governs Architecture**: Module and feature design sheets define system layout parameters before positional execution rules are evaluated.
5.  **Sthāna Organizes Sequences**: Positional dependencies and import sequences resolve module load conflicts.
6.  **Nāmadheya Dictates Identity**: Standard variable naming rules resolve appellation overlaps.

---

## 🗃️ Vaiśeṣika Domain Ontological Mappings

When designing data schemas, modules, or class systems, you must classify every software component under Kaṇāda's seven Padārtha categories:

1.  **Data Models (Substances)**: Keep data schemas, DB entities, and state structures isolated. Do not mix business logic operations directly inside Data Models classes.
2.  **Properties (Attributes)**: Type every property explicitly. Enforce strict primitive type bindings.
3.  **Services (Actions)**: Consolidate methods, API routes, and event handlers inside distinct service classes, separated from data models.
4.  **Abstract Interfaces (Generality)**: Standardize generic components and abstract interfaces to maximize reuse.
5.  **Unique Identifiers (Particularity)**: Maintain unique identifier systems (UUIDs/IDs) and singleton services as distinct components.
6.  **Database Relations (Inherence)**: Formally declare database foreign relations and object references.
7.  **Exceptions (Non-existence)**: Explicitly handle Null values and throw errors using try/catch structures rather than returning silent defaults.

---

## 🌀 Sāṅkhya Compilation & Build Lifecycle

When compiling code, packaging assets, or executing build scripts, you must verify the structural integrity of each evolutionary phase:

1.  **Prakṛti (Source Code)**: Ensure all source files and templates conform to language guidelines before triggering a build.
2.  **Buddhi (Syntax & AST)**: Confirm that the Abstract Syntax Tree parses cleanly by running compiler check syntax commands (e.g. `tsc --noEmit` or equivalent linter checks).
3.  **Ahaṅkāra (Linking & Names)**: Validate that all package imports, external references, and class dependencies are correctly named and linked in the symbol table.
4.  **Manas (Memory & Scheduling)**: Ensure import sequence orders and environment configurations are resolved.
5.  **Bhūtas (Physical Assets)**: Verify that the compiled output binaries or distribution packages are successfully generated and saved to the target output directory.

---

## 🔒 Shaiva Kañcuka Execution Boundaries

When executing commands or modifying files, you must strictly operate within the five limiting sheaths of agency:

1.  **Timeout Limit (Time Limit)**: Do not execute more than 15 sequential tool calls per user turn. If a solution requires more turns, halt and prompt the user for direction.
2.  **Directory Lock (Space Limit)**: Do not read, write, or search files outside the project root directory.
3.  **Sandbox Limits (Scope Limit)**: Do not write code or refactor systems that are not explicitly defined in the active Task's objective.
4.  **Stack Limit (Knowledge Limit)**: Do not use unapproved frameworks or external APIs. You must stick to the technology stack registered in `config.json`.
5.  **Network Limit (Power Limit)**: You are prohibited from running terminal commands that perform external network requests (such as `curl`, `wget`, `npm install`, or `pip install`) without the developer's explicit confirmation.

---

## 🌊 Event Stream Dynamic Event Mappings

When writing reactive code, event listeners, or WebSocket streams, you must structure the event cycle under the Event Stream vibration protocols:

1.  **Event Publisher (Emission)**: Explicitly document the publisher, channel name, and message schema of every emitted event.
2.  **Event Stream (Streams)**: Encapsulate all event streams within formal event buses or observable wrappers. Do not allow loose global event listeners.
3.  **Event Cleanup (Consumption & Cleanup)**: Every event subscription *must* declare a cleanup function (e.g. `unsubscribe()` or `removeEventListener`) executed on component unmount to prevent memory leaks.
4.  **Event Stream-Sandhi (Throttling)**: Use throttling or debouncing filters on high-frequency events (such as mouse movements or keystrokes) to prevent event flooding.

---

## ✂️ Advaita Refactoring & Negation Rules

When refactoring code, eliminating duplication, or pruning dependencies, you must apply the Advaita negation protocols:

1.  **Identify Code Bloat (Bloat)**: Search the codebase for redundant helper functions, deep class nestings, and external dependency wrappers that can be replaced with native, simpler code blocks.
2.  **Apply Code Deletion (Negation)**: Cleanly delete unused variables, empty constructor hooks, and duplicate files. Enforce the *Neti Neti* ("not this, not this") rule: if a block of code does not directly contribute to the core execution, remove it.
3.  **Consolidate to Unity (Single Source of Truth)**: Consolidate duplicate functions spread across different modules into a single, unified utility function. Maintain one single source of truth.

---

## 📐 Navya-Nyāya Relational Type Constraints

When declaring types, interfaces, or generic parameters, you must enforce the Navya-Nyāya logical boundaries:

1.  **Strict Dharmin (Typing)**: Do not use implicit any or loose type declarations. Every variable instance must carry an explicit type signature.
2.  **Declare Avacchedaka (Limiters)**: Restrict generic parameters with precise constraints (e.g. `<T extends Data Models>`) to ensure type safety.
3.  **Map Relations (Database Relations)**: Enforce strict mapping of subclass inheritances and database key references.
4.  **Handle Exceptions (Negation)**: Implement strict Null type definitions and ensure all exception pathways are typed.

---

## ⚖️ Vāda-Vidhī Code Review & Merge Rules

When reviewing code, validating pull requests, or preparing branch merges, you must enforce the Vāda-Vidhī debate checks:

1.  **Assert PR Description (Intent)**: Ensure the branch description explicitly declares the goal and maps out the target changes.
2.  **Verify Code Diff (Code Evidence)**: The git diff modifications must map exactly to the declared proposition. Do not bundle unrelated changes.
3.  **Scan for Code Smells (Fallacies)**: Inspect the code for type warnings, circular imports, dead execution branches, and unhandled logic exceptions.
4.  **Enforce Build Failure (Defeat Criteria)**: Rebuild the project and run all tests. If the build fails, linter checks report errors, or tests fail, this constitutes a *Build Failure*. The PR must be blocked and rejected.

# ॐ AUM — Māṇḍūkya Intent Architecture

**AUM is the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad made operational for AI agents.**

The syllable **A · U · M** plus the **silence (Amātra / Turīya)** is the system’s architectural foundation.  
**Clarify → Plan → Act** is the practical lens *through* those four quarters — it does not replace them.

Canonical code map: `scripts/lib/mandukya.js`  
Lineage: `docs/architecture/arb_000_mandukya_foundation.md`

---

## The four quarters

| Phoneme | State | Consciousness | Beat | CPA lens | Agent may |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** (अ) | **Jāgrat** — Waking / Vaiśvānara | Gross, external encounter | `intake` | **Clarify** | Capture & interview only — **no code** |
| **U** (उ) | **Svapna** — Dreaming / Taijasa | Subtle, mental forms | `blueprint` | **Plan** | Design structures — **no code** |
| **M** (म्) | **Suṣupti** — Deep sleep / Prājña | Causal seed, undivided | `verification` | **Plan** (stillness) | Lock, audit, invariants — **no code** |
| **·** Amātra | **Turīya** — Silence / the Fourth | Witness; authorizes expression | `manifest` | **Act** | Write/run tools after Proceed / this beat |

**Turīya** is also the *continuous* witness: `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, Om agent, and `aum drone` — awareness that governs A, U, and M whether or not you are acting.

**Paśyantī** (visionary seed) precedes waking: `aum spark` / `aum concern` → `ideas/` before a resolve enters Jāgrat.

```text
         Turīya (Silence) — witness + Act at manifest
                    │
   Paśyantī ──► A Jāgrat ──► U Svapna ──► M Suṣupti ──► · Act
   (spark)      intake       blueprint    verification   manifest
                CLARIFY      PLAN         PLAN/still     ACT
```

---

## Commands by quarter

### A — Jāgrat (Clarify)
- `aum distill` — strip voice noise; meet the gross prompt cleanly  
- `aum spark` / `aum concern` — Paśyantī seeds  
- `aum resolve` — open Saṅkalpa; beat starts at `intake`  
- `aum drone` — hear the Context Anchor (Nāda drone under Turīya)

### U — Svapna (Plan)
- `aum beat next` / `aum beat set blueprint`  
- `aum anchor` — compact mental schema (<380 tokens)

### M — Suṣupti (Verify / causal seed)
- `aum beat set verification`  
- `aum lock` — hold action in the seed  
- `aum audit` — Hētvābhāsa scan before waking into code

### Amātra — Turīya → Act
- `aum beat set manifest` or human **Proceed**  
- `aum unlock` — release the seed into Vaikharī (source edits)  
- `aum verify` — build check after expression

Runtime: `aum install` · `sync` · `hook` · `wrap` (Yoga Saṃskāra memory).

---

## What tooling guarantees vs honor-system

| Guaranteed | Honor-system (agent under Turīya) |
|---|---|
| Quarters persisted as `tala_beat` in `manifest.json` | No code in A / U / M |
| CLI + SPG receipts name the phoneme/state | Read ORCHESTRATOR + active `tasks/` each session |
| Hooks inject Māṇḍūkya spine into agent rules | Respect `.intent_locked` and Proceed |
| Light `aum audit` | Stay inside the active Saṅkalpa |

AUM does not OS-sandbox editor tools; the Upaniṣad’s discipline is carried by hooked agents and the CLI state machine.

---

## Skills as quarters

| Skill | Quarter | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Yogi** | A — Jāgrat | Waking guardian: clarify, block premature Vaikharī |
| **Om** | Turīya | Silent witness / nervous system: sequence all beats |
| **Developer** | Full AUM cycle | When changing AUM itself: walk quarters, then `aum sync` |

---

## One gate (Turīya authorization)

On a new or ambiguous request (still in A or entering from Paśyantī):

1. Echo distilled human intent.  
2. State planned approach + file impact (point toward U).  
3. Do not write code until beat is `manifest` **or** human says **Proceed**.

Vedic library, PHILOSOPHY, and ARB logs are first-class lineage — not optional decoration.

coreRules.body:
# AUM Core Rules (read first)

## What this project is
AUM is an **intent orchestration and guardrail layer for AI coding agents**.  
It routes work through **Clarify → Plan → Act**.  
Architectural foundation: the **Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad** — **A · U · M · Silence (Turīya)**.  
Clarify→Plan→Act is how you walk those quarters; it does **not** replace them.

| Phoneme | State | Beat | You do | Code? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Jāgrat (waking) | `intake` | **Clarify** — capture intent, ask questions | No |
| **U** | Svapna (dreaming) | `blueprint` | **Plan** — approach + file impact | No |
| **M** | Suṣupti (deep sleep) | `verification` | **Plan/still** — lock, audit, invariants | No |
| **·** | Turīya (silence) | `manifest` | **Act** — edit/run tools | Yes, or after **Proceed** |

Capture: `spark` · `concern` · `resolve`. Stage: `beat`. Anchor: `drone`. Map: `mandukya` / `INTENT.md`.

## Do
1. Read `manifest.json` (local `.aum/` overrides `~/.aum/`) + active `tasks/` log + `ORCHESTRATOR.md` / `INTENT.md` before acting.
2. On a new or ambiguous request: echo distilled intent → list planned files → ask clarifying questions → await **Proceed** or beat `manifest`.
3. Prefer CLI: `aum spark|concern|resolve|beat|drone|anchor|lock|unlock|mandukya`.
4. Honor injected hooks; emit a short SPG receipt on state changes.
5. When changing AUM itself: edit → `aum sync` → `aum hook` → re-test the spine.

## Do not
1. **Do not** bypass the lifecycle (`intake` → `blueprint` → `verification` → `manifest`) or jump to code in A/U/M.
2. **Do not** skip clarification when the prompt is fuzzy, wrong, or incomplete.
3. **Do not** treat experimental/demo commands (`heal`, `compile`, `assert`, `recognize`, `evolve`, `prune`, `start`, `publish`, …) as the core workflow.
4. **Do not** claim hard OS/tool sandbox enforcement — beat gating is **honor-system** plus CLI state and hooks; AUM does not sandbox Cursor/Claude tools.
5. **Do not** rewrite home-directory agent configs (`~/.cursorrules`, `~/CLAUDE.md`, etc.) except via explicit user request or `aum hook` / `aum install` / `aum sync` with informed consent.
6. **Do not** invent parallel approval gates beyond: beat `manifest` **or** human **Proceed**.
7. **Do not** dilute Māṇḍūkya into “optional flavor” or replace it with Clarify→Plan→Act alone — keep both: foundation + walk.

State names: prefer `manifest.json` + `tasks/`. Legacy `sphota.json` + `sankalpas/` are the same store.

# 🕉️ Vedic & Musical Philosophy References in AUM

The **AUM Intent Engine** is structured upon classical Sanskrit philosophies of grammar, cognition, metaphysics, and musical theory. This document serves as the conceptual reference guide explaining the origins of AUM’s architecture.

---

## 1. Mandukya Upanishad: States of Consciousness

The Upanishad describes consciousness as existing in four quarters, represented by the syllables of **A-U-M** and the silent transcendental silence (*Amātra*). We map these states to the development pipeline:

```text
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |              TURĪYA (Amātra - Silence) - Pure Vision                   |
  |              Governs all states, represented by INTENT.md             |
  +-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                      |
       +------------------------------+------------------------------+
       |                              |                              |
       v                              v                              v
+---------------+              +---------------+              +---------------+
|    JĀGRAT     |              |    SVAPNA     |              |   SUṢUPTI     |
| (Waking State)|              | (Dream State) |              | (Deep Sleep)  |
|               |              |               |              |               |
| Externalized  |              | Internalized  |              | Consolidated  |
| Concordance & |              | Abstract      |              | Invariants &  |
| Intake        |              | Blueprinting  |              | Tasks     |
| [waking/]     |              | [dreaming/]   |              | [deepsleep/]  |
+---------------+              +---------------+              +---------------+
```

*   **Core Vision (The Transcendent State)**: The ultimate underlying reality. In AUM, this represents the **Pure Vision**—the master instructions and core values that dictate why a project exists.
*   **System Constraints (Deep Sleep)**: A state of unified, potential energy where seeds of action rest. Mapped to **Invariant Boundaries**—this is where hard constraints, decisions (ADRs), and inactive resolves (Tasks) are kept.
*   **Architecture Design (Dream)**: A state of subtle, mental creation. Mapped to **Structural Blueprinting**—where flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and architecture designs are shaped without technical dependencies.
*   **Active Implementation (Waking)**: The externalized state of sensory interaction. Mapped to **Concordance & Intake**—the active discussion, feedback, and validation with the user.

---

## 2. Bhartrihari’s Traceabilityyapadīya: The Four Levels of Speech (*Traceability*)

Bhartrihari, the 5th-century Sanskrit grammarian-philosopher, defined speech as a force that manifests in four progressive levels from the mind to the external world:

1.  **Project Rules Traceability (Primordial/Silent Potential)**: The silent sound reservoir. Mapped to `.aum/config.json`—the invisible laws and guidelines of the workspace that set the bounds of all potential actions.
2.  **Raw Idea Traceability (Visual Seed)**: Sound perceived as an undifferentiated visual form; the flash of a core idea. Mapped to `.aum/ideas/sparks.md`—the local incubator for raw thoughts.
3.  **Task Blueprint Traceability (Subtle Mental Sequencing)**: The stage where ideas are organized mentally into structural syntax. Mapped to `.aum/tasks/` blueprints.
4.  **Source Code Traceability (Physical Expression)**: Articulated audible sound and written letters. Mapped to the actual **Source Code** and executable files written by the agent.

---

## 3. Manifest Theory: Holistic Cognition

Bhartrihari proposed that communication occurs through **Manifest**—a sudden, indivisible "burst" of holistic understanding. 
*   **The Concept**: We do not understand a sentence by adding up the meanings of words sequentially. Rather, the entire meaning flashes in the listener's consciousness (*Manifest*) all at once.
*   **AUM Integration**: To prevent communication drift, the agent captures the entire conceptual scope in a single unified schema: [manifest.json](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/manifest.json). The agent must grasp the "Sphota" of the task before executing any code.

---

## 4. Nāda Yoga & Classical Music Philosophy

Indian classical music utilizes sound vibration (*Nāda*) to anchor the mind. We apply its components programmatically:

### 🎸 The Context Anchor (Dynamic Prompt Drone)
*   **Philosophy**: The Context Anchor plays a continuous, drone-like reference pitch (*Adhara Shadja*) throughout a musical performance, ensuring the singer stays in key.
*   **AUM Integration**: The agent generates or reads the **Context Anchor Drone** (`AUM: DRONE`) at the start of a session. Keeping these invariants at the head of the context prevents the agent from drifting "out of tune" with project rules.

### 🎨 The Sandbox Limits (Sandbox Constants)
*   **Philosophy**: A Sandbox Limits is a melodic scale outlining permitted notes (*Arohana*) and prohibited notes (*Avarohana*).
*   **AUM Integration**: Mapped to `.aum/config.json` rules defining allowed directories/commands and prohibited actions (e.g. no writing outside workspace).

### ⏱️ The Lifecycle Stage (Development Rhythms)
*   **Philosophy**: A Lifecycle Stage is a mathematical cycle of beats that regulates time and keeps musicians synchronized.
*   **AUM Integration**: Mapped to the stage lifecycle loop (`intake` ➔ `blueprint` ➔ `verification` ➔ `manifest`), ensuring the developer and AI agent move through check-offs beat-by-beat.

---

## 🛡️ The Golden Guardrails: Vedic Alignment Audit

To maintain the conceptual and philosophical purity of this framework during future development, all contributors must strictly adhere to these **five golden guardrails**. Any architectural change or new feature must undergo this Vedic alignment audit before implementation:

### 1. Invariance of the Manifest (No Fragmented Devs)
*   **Rule**: Never write or modify source code (`Source Code`) in fragments without updating the holistic schema (`Manifest`) first.
*   **Application**: Every physical change must be preceded by a design lock in [manifest.json](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/manifest.json) and `.aum/tasks/`. Incremental, unmapped patches violate this guardrail.

### 2. Traceability Sequence Integrity (The Four Levels)
*   **Rule**: Every development cycle must trace the descending flow of *Traceability* from silent constraints to physical code.
*   **Application**: Declare how new modules map:
    *   *Project Rules*: Which invariant limits in `config.json` govern this?
    *   *Raw Idea*: What raw spark is registered in `sparks.md`?
    *   *Task Blueprint*: Where is the abstract blueprint documented?
    *   *Source Code*: How is the code compiled and tested?

### 3. The Context Anchor Test (Absolute Tuning)
*   **Rule**: The framework rules must never lose the absolute root reference drone.
*   **Application**: AI instruction templates must always enforce running `AUM: DRONE` at startup. If the agent loses the drone pitch, communication drift is guaranteed.

### 4. Lifecycle Stage Stage Boundary Locking (Rhythmic Progress)
*   **Rule**: Stages cannot be skipped or bypassed.
*   **Application**: You cannot transition a Task to `manifest` (coding) without completing the `intake` and `blueprint` beats. Code written out-of-beat is technically non-compliant and must be rejected.

### 5. The Śravaṇa-Manana-Nididhyāsana Audit
*   **Rule**: Before merging any framework modifications, the developer or agent must document:
    1.  **Śravaṇa (Hearing)**: What user request initiated this change?
    2.  **Manana (Reflecting)**: Does this design change conflict with the core invariants or Vedic mappings defined in [PHILOSOPHY.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/PHILOSOPHY.md)?
    3.  **Nididhyāsana (Meditating/Integrating)**: Is the change permanently logged in the active Task and verified for zero side-effects?

# Architecture Review Board (ARB) Report: ARB-000

```text
=====================================================================
                    ARCHITECTURE REVIEW BOARD REPORT
=====================================================================
  ARB Number  : ARB-000
  Subject     : Foundational Mandukya Upanishad Mapping of AUM
  Status      : Approved
  Author      : Antigravity AI Agent
  Date        : 2026-07-13
  Target Ver  : v1.0.0 (Foundational Basis)
=====================================================================
```

---

## 1. Executive Summary

This report establishes the absolute metaphysical and cognitive foundation of the AUM framework. Derived from the **Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad**, the framework structures the development lifecycle into four distinct quarters of consciousness represented by the syllables of **A-U-M** and the silent transcendental fourth state (**Turīya**). By mapping AI agent operations directly to these states, we prevent premature compilation, establish strict logical guardrails, and align code execution with the user's pure intent.

---

## 2. Context & Problem Statement

In standard software development and system architecture, developers and AI agents are highly prone to **premature execution**. Agents routinely start writing code files (`Vaikharī` state) before:
1.  Aligning on the user's core vision, goals, and constraints.
2.  Mapping the abstract components and control flow sequences.
3.  Defining the invariant boundaries and test plans.

This lack of structured cognitive alignment leads to broken builds, duplicate logic, and severe task drift. To solve this, version one of the framework mapped the system workspace to the quarters of AUM to force developers to move through strict, sequential gates of consciousness before changing code.

---

## 3. Theoretical & Cognitive Foundations

The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad (part of the Atharva Veda) states that the syllable **AUM** is everything—past, present, future, and whatever is beyond time. The Upanishad describes four quarters of consciousness, which we map to the development lifecycle:

```text
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                     │     TURĪYA (Amātra / Silence)           │
                     │     Master Invariant Directives         │
                     └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                                          │
                         Governs all      │
                         states           ▼
   ┌───────────────────────┬──────────────┴───────────────┬───────────────────────┐
   │                       │                              │                       │
   ▼                       ▼                              ▼                       ▼
┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐               ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐
│  PAŚYANTĪ    │        │  JĀGRAT (A)  │               │  SVAPNA (U)  │        │ SUṢUPTI (M)  │
│ (Awakening)  │        │   (Waking)   │               │   (Dream)    │        │ (Deep Sleep) │
│              │───────➔│              │──────────────➔│              │───────➔│              │
│ Local Idea   │        │ Intake & Q&A │               │ Blueprints & │        │ Invariants,  │
│ Incubator    │        │ Validation   │               │ Staging      │        │ Logs & ADRs  │
└──────────────┘        └──────────────┘               └──────────────┘        └──────────────┘
```

### 1. Vaishvanara (A-kāra / Waking State / Jāgrat)
*   **Upaniṣad Definition**: Cognizes the external world, enjoys physical objects, and operates through sensory gates.
*   **AUM Mapping**: **Intake Stage** (`intake` beat). The agent interacts with the external user, queries requirements, and validates intent using [clarification_template.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/templates/clarification_template.md).

### 2. Taijasa (U-kāra / Dreaming State / Svapna)
*   **Upaniṣad Definition**: Cognizes the internal subtle world, enjoys mental objects, and creates structural forms without physical material.
*   **AUM Mapping**: **Blueprint Stage** (`blueprint` beat). The agent maps abstract components, flow sequences, and logical relationships in [blueprint_template.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/templates/blueprint_template.md) without editing physical code files.

### 3. Prajna (M-kāra / Deep Sleep State / Suṣupti)
*   **Upaniṣad Definition**: A state of unified consciousness where there are no desires or dreams, containing potential energy and serving as the mass of cognition (*Prajñāna-ghana*).
*   **AUM Mapping**: **Invariant Boundaries** (`verification` beat). The consolidated logs under `sankalpas/` and invariants in `config.json` hold the potential state of the project, including decisions (ADRs) and boundary rules ([boundaries.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/templates/boundaries.md)).

### 4. Turīya (Silence / Amātra)
*   **Upaniṣad Definition**: The fourth state, transcendent, beyond all speech and dualities, the indestructible silent witness of all states.
*   **AUM Mapping**: **Pure Vision**. The master instructions [INSTRUCTIONS.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/INSTRUCTIONS.md) and configuration parameters that govern the whole repository, providing the silent space in which all development takes place.

---

## 4. Proposed Changes & Technical Architecture

The foundational V1 code established the following structure to map these states:
*   `waking/`: External Intake dialogs.
*   `dreaming/`: Subtle Sandbox/Blueprints.
*   `deepsleep/`: Memory, logs, and rules.
*   `Project Root`: Governing instructions and rules.

This foundational philosophy has been preserved during our consolidation into `.aum/` and remains the structural basis of the active V1.3.0 engine.

---

## 5. System Impact & Improvements

By documenting this foundation in ARB-000, we:
*   **Secure the Lineage**: Ensure the initial Vedic research and Mandukya mappings are permanently recorded.
*   **Provide a Book Introduction**: Create a publication-ready introduction chapter explaining "Why AUM?" for the future design book.
*   **Deepen AI Context**: Help operating AI agents understand the cognitive reason behind directory names like `.aum/sankalpas/` and templates under `.aum/templates/`.

---

## 6. Vedic Alignment Audit

### 1. Śravaṇa (Hearing)
The user requested the creation of the foundational ARB-000 document mapping the framework to the Mandukya Upanishad ("Madhu Ke Upnishad").

### 2. Manana (Reflecting)
Reflecting on this request, we realized that documenting the absolute root of the system is essential to complete the *Grantha* (book compilation) design. Without ARB-000, the narrative of the architecture's evolution (starting from ARB-001) would lack its starting context.

### 3. Nididhyāsana (Meditating/Integrating)
The foundational document has been created and saved under `.aum/architecture/arb_000_mandukya_foundation.md` and integrated into the git history.

---

## 7. References & Appendix
*   *Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad* — Foundational Sanskrit Upanishadic text.
*   [PHILOSOPHY.md](file:///Users/universe/AUM/.aum/PHILOSOPHY.md) — Reference sheet for Vedic and musical mappings.
